title: Vision as a core chassis axis — Frames are blind giants, vehicles are their eyes
summary: Use Foundry VTT's native vision/detection system as a real mechanical axis on the campaign map: Frames have poor vision, vehicles range from equally poor to extremely good, and the trade is physical — a sports car sees well precisely because it isn't armoured, while recon vehicles and helicopters have the best sensing of anything on the field. Makes vehicles matter for reasons beyond survivability.
description:
Stated directly while accepting the (since retired) scale-and-chassis proposal: 'a key element of this would be that we use Foundry VTT's vision related stuff so that we create a campaign map where Frames have poor vision, vehicles range from equally poor to extremely good. A sports car has good wide vision because it's not armoured, a recon vehicle has by far the best vision capabilities alongside things like helicopters.'

Why this is more than flavour: chassis are balanced on survivability, speed, and capacity (first in the retired scale-and-chassis design, now in frame.schema.json and chassis.schema.json). Vision adds a fourth axis that is genuinely orthogonal to all three, and it inverts the armour trade — the *least* protected chassis often sees best, because vision loss is a direct physical consequence of armour (slits, hatches, hull). That means a player choosing the fragile option gets a real, non-consolation reward rather than just 'you go fast.'

The resulting battlefield dynamic is strong and thematically on-point: **Frames are enormously powerful and nearly blind.** They physically cannot see what is happening at ground level. So a Frame without spotters is a giant swinging at what it's told about. That makes the vehicle layer structurally necessary rather than merely supportive, so vehicle players are never second-line, and it does so through the map rather than through numbers.

Foundry-side, this is well-supported natively and is a real reason to invest in the module's scene generation: token vision modes, detection modes, sight ranges/angles, and per-token light. A wide-angle low-range configuration (sports car), a narrow-angle long-range configuration (recon/helicopter), and a heavily restricted configuration (buttoned-up Frame or APC) are all expressible in the Token document without custom code. Needs confirming against the local foundryvtt/ tree before it is treated as designed rather than intended.

Connects to the already-accepted world-map-satellite-combat idea (a zoomed-out city map is exactly where limited vision creates fog-of-war decisions) and to automated-recall-knowledge-system (both are about controlling what information reaches which player and when).
sourceContext: User message accepting the (since retired) scale-and-chassis proposal, 2026-08-22, alongside three chassis decisions (auto-levelling, reserve chassis allowed, vehicles as a full parallel progression path).
openSubQuestions: Exact Foundry vision/detection configuration per chassis class — needs verifying against the local foundryvtt/ source tree, not assumed.

Whether Frames' poor vision is a flat sight-range limit, an angle restriction, or a detection-mode restriction (can't detect Medium-or-smaller creatures at all). (The removed frame-scale simulator's engine/vision.mjs used the third for its AI-facing model, but that was a simulator implementation choice, not a decision about what the real Foundry module does for human players.)
Whether vision degrades as a chassis takes damage (a Broken vehicle losing sensors would be thematically strong and mechanically punishing).
How this interacts with night/weather Contacts and with the Claimants' own senses.
resolvedSubQuestions: How spotting is communicated between players in practice, answered 2026-08-23: not just passive not-seeing — an active tool. 'We should limit players in the Foundry scene to the visible areas their mech can see. We should give recon units points that mean they can point to tiles on the map and highlight grid tiles, we literally build the spotting and recon actions into the information which gets to Frame pilots who then have to trust their team and move into a position that is ideal.' Captured as its own idea, foundry-vision-restricted-spotting, since it's a concrete enough mechanic (per-player scene vision restriction + a recon marking tool) to track and design separately from this idea's broader vision-as-an-axis framing.
reconfirmedNote: RECONFIRMED 2026-09-20, unprompted and in almost the same words: "I've written very early on that we will make sight a very important part of the system, all players share vision together but longer range weapons will need other vehicles or frames to be close enough to the enemy to see them. Recon vehicles excel at this task as do helicopters, but recon vehicles are very good at sneaking and hiding whereas helicopters are extremely bad at this." NEW DETAIL beyond the original entry: all players SHARE vision, and the stealth axis is explicitly separate from the sight axis -- recon vehicles are good at both, helicopters are excellent at seeing and terrible at not being seen. Vision and stealth fields are now real on frame.schema.json and chassis.schema.json. The two stale refs this note used to flag (the Sensor Operator ground role, cut 2026-09-20, and the retired scale-and-chassis design) were taken out of the text on 2026-09-25; the chassis axes that design balanced are now carried by the two machine schemas.
